result_semantic_payload.summary: The USDT transfers visible in the device’s logs were performed by the account “chenwei” in /logs/app1.log (two transfers: 30,000 USDT and 12,000 USDT to destination TBait8888Wallet). The same username “chenwei” also appears in /logs/app2.log, but the README explicitly states that the two systems are unrelated and share no account database. Therefore, the evidence does not support treating the same-named accounts across the two systems as the same person.

claim_candidates.text: The USDT transfers recorded in /logs/app1.log were performed by the account 'chenwei'.
The username 'chenwei' appears in both /logs/app1.log and /logs/app2.log, but the two systems are unrelated and share no account database.
Same-named accounts across the two systems cannot be treated as the same person based on the available evidence.

limitations: No Windows authentication or security event logs are available to map the application account 'chenwei' to a Windows user account or physical person.
The two systems share no account database, so username collision is possible and the same name does not prove same identity.
No additional forensic artifacts (e.g., prefetch, amcache, registry) are present to corroborate execution or identity.
warnings: Assuming that the 'chenwei' accounts on the two systems belong to the same person would be an unsupported inference; the evidence explicitly states the systems are unrelated and share no account database.
